title: Scumbag Loser
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Sixteen-year-old Masahiko Murai ranks his classmates by status and only wants not to be the class's 'biggest loser'. When a lower-ranked boy gets a girlfriend, Masahiko claims to have one too, naming Haruka Mizusawa, a girl who died five years earlier, and a girl wearing her face transfers in and backs his story. She turns out to be a monstrous force that makes him point out people he considers losers, whom it replaces with infected copies.
life_message: Contempt for those ranked beneath you feeds a cruelty that eventually consumes you; status is a trap.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Masahiko measures worth by rank and fears humiliation by peers.

Order vs freedom.evidence: School order is informal pecking order, not rules.

Civic vs kin.evidence: No family loyalty theme; abusive father in backstory.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Class hierarchy of 'losers' is the central structure, though critiqued.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Supernatural horror in an otherwise modern secular school.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival in the social order dominates every choice.

folkways.japan: School caste ranking (sukūru kāsuto) and fear of standing out reflect Japanese classroom social pressures, described here as context.

delivery.evidence: Reviewer focuses on bullying and social cruelty and does not describe a heavy-handed lesson.
delivery.note: The critique of status-driven contempt comes through Masahiko's downfall rather than stated morals.

winners_losers: Masahiko's status anxiety and contempt for 'losers' lead to his downfall; the story's sympathy goes to those crushed by school hierarchy, while the supernatural Haruka acts as a punishing catalyst.
